findings.summary: verify() compares cost run ids against pool run ids that record_cost copied from the same entry run_ids that select_runs set from pool_ids, and line 737 compares run_ids_source against the identical constant select_runs wrote, so neither fails on a code regression; only the summary-scope-id intersection at :757 is an independent source.
if scope.get('outside_roster') passes when scope_check is absent, so a record carrying no out-of-family comparison clears the gate whose done-when requires that comparison.

verify() asserts only that the convergence element id exists, so a fragment reading Converged yes on an unstamped family would pass; line 826 prints the verdict from stamped alone, disagreeing with render()'s definition at :522 which also requires no below-threshold, fallen or unscored member.

below_ref is computed and counted at :828 but never compared against the fragment, so the done-when clause that members below 0.85 are named is unasserted; it passes today only because the fragment names none.

roster_check records positive_control_match_count but never compares it to POSITIVE_CONTROL_EXPECTED, so a roster search that read nothing would still set valid_non_west true and the fragment would claim a real absence on an empty search; the sibling enforced this with a raise.

fixture() asserts only below_threshold naming and is never invoked by verify, so it guards the library docs_score_regressions rather than the inline a<b comparison render() and verify() actually use; the sibling also asserted the fell list and that an unchanged column reported nothing.

halted is false and halt_reasons null while the embedded summary at line 138 says halted true with two reasons, because FAMILY_STATUS matches nothing in the wrapped apply log and record_apply reads that regex rather than entry result; the fragment is correct only through its summary fallback.
